races.name: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sandret
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a genuine hold-up style and two recent wins over 8f on Good ground; Sam England has been firing at a modest but respectable rate, and 29 days off is fine — the concern is whether this 1m2f trip on a flat track extracts the same finishing effort he has shown at shorter.|

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who sets the entire tactical picture; Tim Easterby's yard is in excellent form (8/87 at 14 days) and the horse holds a headgear flag, has winning form on Good, and ran just 10 days ago — fitness is not a worry, and uncontested lead over 1m2f on fast ground is exactly what this profile needs.|

runners_data.name: Stipulation
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose last five runs show a pattern of failing to land blows in similar handicap company; the 1m2f-plus trip is clearly the right territory given the 10f-12f history, but recent form figures of 33867 suggest the spark is missing even when the conditions align.|

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished in the frame in four of her last five starts over 8f-10f on Good ground; Tim Easterby's second string here, but the 14-day turnaround and headgear flag suggest she is fit and ready, and she is one of the two most likely to secure the prominent spot behind Perfidia.|

runners_data.name: Alazwar
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the volume of similarly-styled runners in this field means he will not get his preferred rearward berth; the 43-day absence and trainer's blank 14-day strike rate add further caution, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence even if the race shape were ideal.|

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr has been solid recently (4/20 at 14 days) and Star Start shows good course-form indicators at this 10f trip on Good ground; a true prominent type who is well-placed to contest the second or third spot from the outset, making her one of the better-placed horses if the controlled-pace shape plays out.|

runners_data.name: Little She
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer in profile but pushed into a midfield mapping because the field is saturated with pace; Marcus Tregoning's four-year-old has placed twice from five recent runs, including a second on Soft, and the headgear flag is noted — the STYLE_FIT discount applies here because she cannot realistically dominate the prominent ground.|

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's six-year-old is a hold-up type by inclination yet finds himself boxed into a midfield slot by the sheer density of similar profiles in this race; only seven days since his last run is an eyecatcher for fitness, but his recent form includes a U (unseated) and figures of 6/14f suggest the step up to longer trips has not consistently delivered, and the trainer's 0/18 at 14 days is a negative flag.|

races.paceDynamic: Perfidia is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Beverley, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any genuine challenger for the lead — Sunny Orange and Star Start are the nearest prominent types but neither has the profile to seriously pressure Perfidia for the front. This creates a controlled, single-file race from flag to flag, with the pace likely to be honest enough on this flat 1m2f trip to keep hold-up horses honest, but not truly searching. The field contains more prominent and hold-up horses than the map can accommodate naturally: Little She, Alazwar, and The Pug are all genuine positional types who will be unable to secure their preferred berths, with Sunny Orange and Star Start most likely to lock in the prominent slots behind Perfidia. The tactical verdict here favours horses who can race close to the controlled pace and travel within themselves — specifically prominent and close-tracking profiles — as the steady but uncontested gallop set by Perfidia will reward those who do not give ground away early and can deliver sustained, rather than explosive, finishes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Perfidia Controls, Prominent Pair Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Perfidia leads uncontested and sets a fair but manageable pace, allowing Sunny Orange and Star Start to track comfortably.
scenarios.body: Perfidia dictates every yard from a position of complete authority, and the prominent trackers behind benefit from covering minimal ground and arriving at the business end full of racing; the Good to Firm surface rewards those who have been close throughout rather than those asked to produce a big late run from off the pace. This is the dominant shape — a clean, processional race where positional advantage at halfway translates directly into finishing position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Perfidia Dictates, Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Perfidia's gallop is just fast enough to string out the field, allowing one of the genuine hold-up types to deliver late from a true rearward position.
scenarios.body: Sandret, who has the strongest hold-up profile and recent winning form, would be the principal beneficiary if the pace is sufficient to create a gap between the winner and the prominent bunch; on Good to Firm ground she has demonstrated she can finish with purpose. The scenario requires the pace to be faster than expected given Perfidia's tendency to find a comfortable rhythm, making this a secondary rather than primary shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Prominent Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Sunny Orange or Star Start pushes up to dispute the lead and unsettles Perfidia's rhythm, creating a more pressured gallop.
scenarios.body: A faster pace than expected would compress finishing times and reward horses with tactical versatility, potentially exposing Perfidia late; Sunny Orange's consistent prominent form and Tim Easterby's yard in good nick make this a credible if not dominant threat. However this outcome relies on horses racing in a slightly more competitive manner than their individual profiles suggest, and the benefit remains with those positioned ahead of midfield.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Surprise Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and jostles for position early, leaving the redistributed types — Alazwar, The Pug, Little She — stuck further back than their adjusted map positions imply.
scenarios.body: These three are true hold-up or prominent horses racing out of role, and even in a scrambled race they are unlikely to produce decisive late moves given trip, going, and the steady nature of Perfidia's likely gallop; this scenario is assigned low probability precisely because it depends on horses tagged as out of role delivering against their current positional disadvantage. An unexpected result from this group would require a material pace collapse that the data does not support.

watchPoints.text: Perfidia's ability to lead uncontested without any early challenge is the single biggest factor shaping this race — if she clears cleanly from the gates, the entire race is run to her rhythm and the prominent tracking pair become the primary beneficiaries.|

Sunny Orange and Star Start could create a mild jostle for the prominent slots behind Perfidia in the first furlong; if either pushes up and forces an earlier-than-expected pace, the race shape shifts meaningfully away from Scenario A.|

Sandret's hold-up style is legitimate, but on a flat Beverley track over 1m2f with a steady front-runner, watch whether he gets enough pace to aim at — if the gallop is truly sedate, his finishing effort may arrive too late to matter.|

Alazwar, The Pug, and Little She are all racing at least partially out of positional role today — if any one of them gets shuffled wide or loses ground at the start, the gap to bridge on Good to Firm ground will be significant given Perfidia's likely metronomic pace.|

The going report consistently lists this 1m2f as Good to Firm, which rewards prominent and pace-positive profiles — horses with a history of finishing strongly on the quicker end of Good ground (Perfidia, Sunny Orange) carry a surface advantage over those whose best form came on Soft or Standard.|

races.name: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Porter's Song
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Liam Bailey but form reads 5-5659 with no wins or places on similar going in four attempts; 50-day absence is a flag and Jack Garritty takes over in the saddle, making this one to treat cautiously.|

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's yard is in solid form at 4/19 over 14 days; genuinely a rear-division horse placed to midfield on the map due to the density of hold-up types, so its natural late run may be squeezed — two places from 15 similar-ground runs shows consistency without dominance.|

runners_data.name: La Trinite
runners_data.note: Neil King fields two here and La Trinite brings the most relevant recent form: a runner-up at 12f on Good ground and a third at 16f on Soft suggest the trip suits; naturally a closer whose race positioning may be compromised by the congested hold-up field.|

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Second King runner, a six-year-old mare who wears a hood (p) and whose 0-9760 recent form is unpromising; four runs between 16f and 24f suggest she stays the trip well, but her natural style is deep hold-up and she sits mapped to midfield by necessity — that positional squeeze could cost her.|

runners_data.name: Ruler Of The River
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's runner wears a tongue-strap and cheekpieces (tp), which adds an unknown dimension; one win and three places from 15 similar-going runs is a decent strike rate among this group, and 1W3P on Good ground makes him one of the better going-fit profiles despite his 13-day turnaround.|

runners_data.name: Talking In Kode
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Edward Bethell's yard who wears a visor (v) and is 0W1P from seven Good-ground runs — his entire form profile is on this going, which is a significant positive; the step up from 10f to 12f on the map needs proving but the visor application may sharpen his response in a sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Head Girl
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's three-year-old wears a hood (p) and showed a place at 12f on Good ground among her recent runs; naturally a hold-up filly whose form 67-939 is modest, and with the redistribution meaning she won't get her preferred rear position naturally, she may lack the tactical flexibility to overcome the positional challenge.|

races.paceDynamic: This 1m4f Beverley contest on Good to Firm ground is a peculiar shape: every single runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and the field is likely to crawl into the straight before exploding into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. With Porter's Song, Talking In Kode, Character Testing, La Trinite, Blackwater Lilly, Ruler Of The River, and Head Girl all preferring to race off the pace, whoever gets shuffled to the front reluctantly will be doing so against their natural instincts, likely producing a falsely slow early tempo. The race will almost certainly be won by whichever horse picks up sharpest from a dawdling gallop, meaning raw acceleration and a high cruising speed into the straight matter far more than stamina here. This shape strongly favours the horse with the best finishing kick from a compact, bunched field — a true hold-up finisher with a sharp turn of foot on quick ground is the profile to side with, while those who lack that late gear will be found out by the sprint nature of the finale.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and explodes into a bunched sprint over the final two furlongs on the Good to Firm surface.
scenarios.body: With no pace-setter, the tempo will be pedestrian and the race reduced to a flat-out dash home, rewarding the sharpest accelerator from a tight group; Good to Firm ground amplifies the advantage of a quick-twitch finisher.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Gets Gap
scenarios.trigger: If one runner manages to find clear daylight on the outside turning in and sustains a run all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: A horse that angles widest into the straight avoids traffic in the bunched finish and sustains momentum on the fast surface; the compressed pace means getting a clean run is the single biggest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Reluctant Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one runner is nudged or drifts to the front early and, finding themselves alone, builds a small but decisive lead.
scenarios.body: A horse front-running against its nature can still steal the race if rivals are slow to challenge from the back of the pack; the fast ground means any lead built even at a modest pace is hard to reel in if rivals leave their run too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Stoic
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo surges mid-race unevenly, stringing the field out and creating a stamina test rather than a sprint.
scenarios.body: An uneven gallop with a sustained middle section would suit the horse with the best proven form at a mile and a half on good ground, filtering out those relying purely on acceleration.

watchPoints.text: Talking In Kode is the only three-year-old in the field and carries the lightest weight at 127lbs — in a sprint finish, that allowance could be decisive if Cian Horgan (5lb claimer) times the run well.|
With all seven runners holding up naturally, watch for severe traffic problems in the straight as the field bunches — horses on the widest outside draw may have a significant advantage.|

Ruler Of The River's cheekpieces and tongue-strap combination (tp) is worth monitoring in the parade ring — if he is fractious or early to settle, that could undermine his chance in a race that requires a clean, controlled hold-up run.|

La Trinite and Blackwater Lilly both run for Neil King — if King's two runners track each other, one may block the other's run, so watch how Dougie Costello and Paul Mulrennan position them relative to each other from the outset.|

Hoof Hustle Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Won over 8f Good 20 days ago in decent form for Edward Bethell and Oisin Orr; prominent style suits tracking Napolian closely on this flat track, and his sim-going figures (5/7 at Good) give him solid course-condition credentials over a trip he is already proven at.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover's yard is in fair nick (T14: 2/5) and Jason Hart partners a horse whose natural hold-up style is genuine; won over 7f Good recently (1/7f/GOO) so the trip is proven, and he is the most authentic closer in the field if any meaningful tempo develops.

runners_data.name: Lady Hornblower
runners_data.note: 67 days off the track is a significant query for a 3yo filly, and Jack Garritty steps in for Jedd O'Keeffe whose yard is 0 from 2 over the 14-day window; her best sim-going form came at SOF rather than the faster ground declared today, adding an additional concern.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: An 8yo with a sharp recent record — won over 7f Good 36 days ago and placed twice more at the trip — Joanna Mason's 3lb claim is useful; M&D Easterby have decent recent numbers (T14: 3/33) and the horse's prominent style suits a race where Napolian sets a fair pace without pressure.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's yard is busy and in form (T14: 4/46); David Nolan takes the ride on this confirmed front-runner whose lone pace advantage is real but whose STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is worth noting given he was a hold-up horse on his last run — if he settles into the lead, that is his best chance, but any hesitation in breaking could unsettle the plan.

runners_data.name: Dumfries
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 6yo has been placed at this trip before and the yard is ticking over (T14: 4/20); naturally a prominent racer whose true role has been displaced here by stronger pace claims — he'll need to secure a position closer to the front than the map suggests if he is to be competitive, though his STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) signals the squeeze.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by inclination whose sim-going figures are modest (11/15, no wins) and who has been redistributed to midfield given the congested rear; Rowan Scott rides for the same O'Meara yard as Napolian, and the 0W in recent sim-going form makes it hard to make a strong case without a more honest gallop to aim at.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Ethan Tindall claims 5lbs for Noel Wilson's small yard (T14: 1/6) and the horse carries headgear (p); a natural hold-up type displaced forward on the pace map, with no wins in recent sim-going form and the lowest OR in the field (52) — the claim helps but the horse needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and on Good to Firm at Beverley over 7½f he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop without any rival willing or able to press him hard. Masaban and Carolus Magnus are the other prominent types likely to track closely just off the pace, giving the race a compact, bunched look in the early stages rather than a strongly-run affair. With Dumfries redistibuted from his natural prominent berth and the hold-up brigade of Norcross Brow, Lady Hornblower, Willowinghurn and Walk On Walk On all needing something to come back to them late, this is a race that sets up primarily for stalkers who can sit within a length or two of the leader and pounce in the straight. The field contains more prominent/hold-up types than the pace map can naturally accommodate — Dumfries, Willowinghurn and Walk On Walk On are genuine pace or hold-up horses pushed out of their true roles — meaning Napolian's chance of dictating a controlled tempo is high and the race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in second or third, close to the fractions, rather than closers relying on a truly searching gallop to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Napolian Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Napolian leads unmolested and the pace is steady enough to suit horses racing second or third throughout.
scenarios.body: Napolian sets a fair clip without being pressed and the prominent trackers Masaban and Carolus Magnus are ideally placed to pounce inside the final furlong; the lack of a genuine pace duel means stamina-sapping fractions never materialise, rewarding horses who can quicken off a sensible tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Napolian's steady fractions allow him to coast into the straight with Masaban or Carolus Magnus never fully reeled in.
scenarios.body: A soft pace turns the final 2½f into a sprint and Napolian, unburdened by a hard early race, finds more in the tank than expected; Carolus Magnus, with two recent wins at 7f Good, is dangerous as a staying-on second if the winner is already gone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively honest and the hold-up horses, despite being shuffled back, manage to generate genuine late momentum.
scenarios.body: Norcross Brow, a genuine hold-up type in natural role, is best placed of the rear contingent having won over 7f Good recently and pairs with Jason Hart's positive forcing tactics; Lady Hornblower's market drift at 67 days off is a concern but her sim-going figures give her a slim claims if stamina counts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Scrambles Early
scenarios.trigger: If Dumfries pushes forward against type and creates a contested early pace, unsettling Napolian's rhythm.
scenarios.body: A scrappy early pace burns off Napolian sooner than expected and opens the door for a fresher mid-division horse to coast through; Norcross Brow and Walk On Walk On, both with 8f Good form, may benefit marginally but this shape relies on horses racing out of role and is inherently less reliable.

watchPoints.text: Napolian's early position is critical — if David Nolan settles him cleanly in front without a rival forcing the issue, he dictates the entire race shape; any hesitation or challenge for the lead from Dumfries in the opening furlong would fundamentally alter the pace dynamic.

Dumfries is mapped to midfield but is a genuine prominent racer — James Sullivan may attempt to push forward regardless, and if he does he puts pressure on Napolian earlier than expected, potentially compressing the advantage for trackers Masaban and Carolus Magnus.

Lady Hornblower's 67-day layoff combined with a trainer who is 0/2 in the 14-day window and ground that may be quicker than her best form warrants makes her a notable risk for those framing multiples — monitor market support at the off.

Carolus Magnus's course-and-distance profile is strong (won 7f Good 36 days ago) and Joanna Mason's 3lb claim reduces his topweight burden to an effective competitive level — if the stalker scenario unfolds he should be prominent at the business end.

Norcross Brow is the standout hold-up horse with genuine credentials at the trip and going, and Jason Hart will be looking to make ground from the turn in — watch whether any sustainable pace develops in the middle stages to give him something to aim at.

races.name: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 6f on good ground and has solid course form; natural prominent racer who should slot in directly behind Empress Olivia and is the most logical pace-presser in this field — strong scenario-A and C candidate.

runners_data.name: Le Beau Garcon
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist returning after 42 days off for Easterby; has placed twice on good ground over 5f but will need genuine pace to close into — trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/33 is modest and the layoff is a minor concern.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Ruth Carr hold-up type coming off 42 days' rest; has twice finished second on good ground over this trip and handles the conditions, but like Le Beau Garcon needs the race truly run to get competitive late — trainer T14 of 4/20 is acceptable.

runners_data.name: Speeding Bullet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 55 days, the longest absence in the field; placed twice on good ground but form figures of 22-077 suggest he needs things to fall perfectly and a genuinely honest gallop to be involved — the freshness is an unknown.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who shapes as the race-maker; the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is racing somewhat out of role as a P-type mapped to lead, but her recent 12-day turnaround for Walford and uncontested lead give her real claims — key to the entire race shape.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: Consistent placer in recent runs (three seconds, two thirds) wearing a visor; a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield map position because the field is saturated with closers — its natural finishing position at the rear may be harder to execute here, tempering its chance.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Won last time out on good ground over 5f eight days ago and returns quickly; fitted with a tongue-strap, and while its hold-up style is compressed into the midfield map, the recent winning momentum and fast turnaround for Rothwell give it residual each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Crafty Spirit
runners_data.note: Won twice in its last five starts including back-to-back victories on good ground over this distance; held up by nature but its excellent recent form is the standout qualifier — the blinkers are retained and it is one of the more dangerous closers if pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose last five runs all came on good ground and who has never won on the turf beyond a 3/15 sim-going record; trainer Jackson has a blank 14-day record (0/4) and the consistent mid-to-rear finishes suggest this shape does not suit — outsider claims only.

races.paceDynamic: Empress Olivia is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 5f Beverley handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a measured, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground that will suit her stamina profile. Azuinthejungle is the only other horse with natural prominent intent and will press forward to track Empress Olivia, but the bulk of the field — Golden Havana, Crafty Spirit, Without Flaw, Opal Storm and Le Beau Garcon — are genuine hold-up types shuffled into midfield by the sheer density of closers in this nine-runner field and will have to navigate traffic rather than simply sit where they please. With pace likely to be controlled and comfortable rather than scorching over 5f on fast ground, the early gallop will not be truly searching, meaning the front two will conserve energy and the closers face an uphill task to generate enough late momentum to run them down. This race shape strongly favours prominent or pace-pressing runners — specifically those with the ability to track a lone leader and quicken from a handy position — over the true hold-up types who are structurally disadvantaged by the lack of a truly contested early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Empress Olivia Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Olivia breaks cleanly and is allowed to set a controlled, solo gallop with Azuinthejungle the only horse in close pursuit, the race is run to suit confirmed front-runners.
scenarios.body: Empress Olivia sets an honest but not suicidal tempo on ground that has been riding fast all day, and the hold-up contingent — shuffled into false midfield positions — never generate enough late zip to reel in the front two.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp The Line
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected due to Azuinthejungle pressing hard and the front pair burning out before the furlong pole, creating a true-run race for the closers.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested gallop compresses finish times and allows the legitimate hold-up horses to close with real purpose; those with recent winning form at this trip on similar ground come into their own.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Surge Together
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle tracks Empress Olivia closely and surges past in the final furlong while the solo leader fades from her uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Azuinthejungle's recent course-and-distance form and good-ground record make her the natural heir to any lead that softens in the closing stages, and she has the class ratings to confirm superiority.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Olivia misses the break or is forced wider than ideal, scrambling the entire pace shape and triggering a messy, falsely-run race.
scenarios.body: In the ensuing chaos, horses with tactical versatility and recent sharp form benefit most, but no single profile holds a clear edge; low-draw handy types are best positioned to capitalise on the disorder.

watchPoints.text: Empress Olivia's break is pivotal — if she misses the stalls or is crowded early, the entire race shape collapses and every probability shifts dramatically toward the hold-up horses.

Crafty Spirit and Opal Storm are both genuine hold-up types running just 8-14 days after their last start — monitor them in the paddock for signs of freshness or fatigue, as their form reads well but their natural style is disadvantaged by the likely pace scenario.

Golden Havana has been placed in five of its last five runs but wears a visor and has a STYLE_FIT flag; if the pace is soft and closers are bottled up in a falsely-run race, its consistent placing record may flatter its actual winning chance here.

Azuinthejungle's jockey Alex Jary claims 3lb, which is significant in a compressed handicap range of OR 53-67 — watch whether the claim proves a decisive weight advantage if the race sets up as a prominent duel with Empress Olivia.

The going is universally Good to Firm across the card at Beverley today, confirmed by six races — the fast surface will sharpen early fractions and may test the stamina of any hold-up horse that cannot get a prominent enough position to challenge.
